items.title: Google Meet is making it easy to download a local copy of the file your host’s presenting
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is adding direct download support to Meet for files shared by presenters. 
 Presenters can link to Google Docs, Sheets, or Slide files they screen-share with call participants. 
 Sharing can be enabled only for specific files, or everything across the call. 

By now, we’ve all probably sat through at least one videoconference where we struggled to follow along with someone presenting a document like a slideshow or PDF, wishing we just had our own copy of the file to look at — and thankfully, Google Meet is now making it a lot easier for us to get our hands on just that.

When a presenter screen-shares a document with the rest of the call, so far Meet hasn’t offered a built-in way to easily distribute copies of that document to call participants. Maybe the best option there has been just dropping a link in chat.

items.title: Android’s controversial sideloading rules go global in January
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google has announced that it will expand Android’s new sideloading and developer verification rules to global markets in January 2027. 
 The company will force all app developers to verify their identities, including apps on the Play Store, Galaxy Store, and several other OEM markets. 
 People who want to sideload unverified apps will need to take plenty of steps, including a 24-hour wait. 

Google announced developer verification and changes to app sideloading last year. These changes started rolling out in four countries back in September, and the search giant has now announced a date for a global expansion.

Google has confirmed a January 2027 global rollout for these new developer rules and sideloading changes:

items.title: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Fitbit Edge owners report that the tracker lacks hourly reminders to move. 
 The tracker still monitors hourly activity but doesn’t vibrate to remind users to reach their 250-step goal. 
 Reminders to move have been available on Fitbit devices since 2016, helping users stay active throughout the day. 

One of the simplest ways Fitbit has helped people stay active over the years is by encouraging them to get out of their chairs. As far back as the original Fitbit Alta in 2016, Fitbit offered reminders to move. Rather than letting you cram all your daily steps into an evening walk, the feature encouraged you to spread your activity throughout the day. However, those upgrading to the new Google Fitbit Edge are discovering that their wrists have gone unusually quiet.

Reports on Reddit , Facebook ( 2 ), and the Google Health Community reveal that the Fitbit Edge lacks an option to enable hourly reminders to move. While the tracker still records hourly activity, it apparently doesn’t vibrate to remind you when you’re falling short of your 250-step hourly goal.
items.t: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders

items.title: Samsung prepares Galaxy AI on Snapdragon X Elite for its upcoming Android laptops
items.summary:
Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals that Samsung is preparing on-device Galaxy AI features for its upcoming Snapdragon X Elite-powered Android laptops, codenamed Origin. 
 Samsung AI Core adds local support for Generative Edit, in-painting and out-painting, and harmonization, while Samsung Semantic Core lists the chip for on-device Gauss language, translation, and vision models. 
 Samsung Video Editor adds a Snapdragon X Elite X1E-80-100 profile with flagship 8K editing limits, alongside new references in Samsung Gallery, and Samsung Device Health Manager. 

Samsung is getting Galaxy AI ready for the Snapdragon X Elite, the chip inside its upcoming Android laptops. Samsung’s on-device AI apps on the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 now list the chip, which we’ve tied to Samsung’s laptops codenamed Origin . The same build also reveals the laptops’ dedicated One UI interface with Circle to Search and how they’ll plug into the Galaxy ecosystem .

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung already sells Windows laptops with the Snapdragon X Elite, like the Galaxy Book4 Edge, and they offer some Galaxy AI features through Windows apps. The new entries in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 are different: they sit in the Android versions of Samsung’s AI apps, so they’re meant for One UI running on the laptop itself.
items.t: Samsung prepares Galaxy AI on Snapdragon X Elite for its upcoming Android laptops

TL;DR

 Agents is a dedicated page in Google Wallet where you can view and monitor all your Gemini purchases. 
 It was officially announced earlier this week, though we spotted development on it for Android over a month ago. 

Last month, we found a new Agents option in Google Wallet’s account switcher menu, and it appears to be rolling out gradually. Agents lets users view and manage their purchases made through Gemini, and it was announced for iOS and the web this week. However, the company didn’t share any visuals of the feature.

We’re now getting a good look at the Agents tab in action, courtesy of the web version of Google Wallet, which shows a new page listing your purchases made via Gemini. There’s also a “Create a task” button that redirects you to the Google Gemini app if no task is listed.

items.title: One UI 9.5 could make booking an Uber part of your Now Brief routine
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Samsung is working on proactive ride-booking suggestions for Now Brief and Now Nudge in One UI 9.5. 
 Your Galaxy phone could suggest booking a ride through Gemini based on your upcoming appointments and departure times. 
 The underlying code references Uber, Lyft, Kakao T, and DiDi as supported ride-hailing apps. 

Say you have a dinner reservation at 7 PM. Samsung’s Now Brief can already remind you about it, show you the restaurant’s location, and let you know when it’s time to leave. But getting there is still your responsibility. You could open Uber or even ask Gemini to book a ride for you. With One UI 9.5 , Samsung appears to be working on connecting those dots so that your Galaxy phone can offer to arrange a ride before you even ask.

Earlier this week, we learned that Samsung is developing a Daily Briefing feature for Now Brief that can automatically generate reminders using information from other apps. Now, an APK teardown by SammyGuru has revealed how Samsung could turn some of those reminders into actionable suggestions.
items.t: One UI 9.5 could make booking an Uber part of your Now Brief routine

items.title: Samsung’s Origin laptops will plug into the Galaxy ecosystem, and One UI is laying the foundation

Credit: Zac Kew-Denniss / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals that Samsung is laying the groundwork in its Android apps to plug its upcoming origin14 and origin16 (likely the XE940 and XE960) laptops into the Galaxy ecosystem. 
 Supported continuity tools could include Call & text on other devices, Multi Control, Storage Share, Galaxy Buds auto-switching, phone-as-a-webcam sharing, instant hotspot sharing with Windows PCs, and offline Find My Mobile tracking. 
 Smart View could also gain Mirror and Extend display modes alongside Second Screen support, while Galaxy AI tools like Now Brief and Now Nudge could get dedicated laptop layouts. 

Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops will plug straight into the Galaxy ecosystem, according to code in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1. We found the laptops’ codenames, origin14 and origin16, earlier today, along with their dedicated One UI laptop interface with Circle to Search , and the same build lays the foundation for adapting most of Samsung’s connected-device features to them.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

Samsung already offers most of these connected-device features on its Windows-based Galaxy Book laptops, through Windows apps. The new strings below are different, though. They sit in the Android versions of Samsung’s apps and refer to “this laptop,” meaning One UI itself is running on the laptop. Several of these apps, including Smart View and Find My Mobile, will also check whether they’re running on a “desktop” class device, the same check…
items.t: Samsung’s Origin laptops will plug into the Galaxy ecosystem, and One UI is laying the foundation

items.title: One UI 9.5 code reveals Samsung’s dedicated Android laptop interface with Circle to Search
items.summary:
Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Code in Samsung’s One UI 9.5 Beta 1 reveals a dedicated interface for its upcoming Android laptops (codenamed origin14 and origin16) that hides Samsung DeX and tablet taskbar settings in favor of a separate laptop UI. 
 The new laptop taskbar will likely include built-in Circle to Search, an AI select button, a phone apps shortcut, auto-hide functionality, and left- or right-aligned navigation buttons. 
 Additional strings across apps point to automatic keyboard backlighting, haptic touchpads, lid-open startup, and laptop-specific power and lock screen prompts. 

Samsung’s upcoming Android laptops will likely have a One UI taskbar with Circle to Search built in, according to code in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 release. We found the laptops’ codenames, origin14 and origin16 , in the same build earlier today, and the beta also shows how Samsung’s software will look and work on them. Samsung is also preparing on-device Galaxy AI features for the laptops’ Snapdragon X Elite chip , and the laptops will plug into the Galaxy ecosystem with calls, Smart View, and Find My Mobile.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

items.title: OpenAI’s first smartphone could launch in 2027 with help from iPhone manufacturer
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has reportedly secured an order to assemble OpenAI’s first smartphone. 
 Several other Apple suppliers are reportedly involved, with the phone potentially launching in late 2027 or 2028. 
 The device is expected to feature a custom MediaTek chip and an AI-first user experience, but its operating system remains unknown. 

For a company whose most recognizable product lives inside an app on your phone, OpenAI appears increasingly interested in making the phone itself. We first heard about its smartphone ambitions in April , and a new report from China suggests the project is making headway with familiar names from Apple’s supply chain.

Citing supply chain sources, Chinese publication Securities Times (via Abhishek Yadav on X ) reports that Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile has secured an order to assemble OpenAI’s smartphone. Foxconn is already one of Apple’s biggest iPhone manufacturing partners, meaning the company could soon have another major smartphone client with roots in Cupertino.
items.t: OpenAI’s first smartphone could launch in 2027 with help from iPhone manufacturer

Apple switched from titanium to aluminum for the frame of the iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max, and stuck with that material for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max this year. However, it looks like aluminum might not live much longer in its top-end lineup.

Today, tipster Fixed Focus Digital took to Weibo to claim that the iPhone 20 Pro will have a curved design, and that early-stage engineering work on a titanium frame for it is already underway. According to the tipster, the frame is somewhat like the one on the iPhone Air, but much more rounded.

items.title: Nvidia halts its H200 chip sales to China
items.summary:
Back in December, Nvidia received government approval to sell its H200 AI chips to specially approved customers in China. That deal had some attached strings, like a 25% export tariff charged by the US, but Nvidia is now completely abandoning its H200 chip exports to China.

During the latest Q3 earnings call, Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, revealed that the company is pausing its H200 shipments to China. There was no official comment as to why Nvidia is ceasing its H200 chip shipments, though it is likely related to former CEO and founder Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Megaspeed...
items.t: Nvidia halts its H200 chip sales to China
